title: Section 152 — Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

content.overview: BNS s. 152 — Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, signs, visible representation, electronic communication, financial means or otherwise, excites secession, armed rebellion, subversive activities, or separatist feelings, or endangers sovereignty or unity. Life, or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
In student language: BNS s. 152 is the rule on “Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India”. The section provides that whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial mean, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India; or indulges in or commits any such act shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 152 exists so that “Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India” has a closed legal test in Chapter VII — Of Offences Against the State. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Waging war, and the new s. 152 on sovereignty, unity and integrity — not a relabel of sedition.

The provision in detail
152. Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial mean, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India; or indulges in or commits any such act shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial mean, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India; or indulges in or commits any such act shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Punishment / legal consequence
Life, or up to 7 years, + fine.

Explanations
Explanation.–Comments expressing disapprobation of the measures, or administrative or other action of the Government with a view to obtain their alteration by lawful means without exciting or attempting to excite the activities referred to in this section do not constitute an offence under this section

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 152 (Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India), Chapter VII — Of Offences Against the State.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial mean, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India; or indulges in or commits any such act shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 152 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Replaces colonial sedition with a modernized constitutional provision criminalizing acts exciting secession, armed rebellion, or subversive activities endangering national sovereignty and unity.

Core Legal Mandate: Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial mean, or otherwise, excites or att...
Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter VII penal tiers.
Evidentiary and Procedural Cognate: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
essentialIngredients: The commission of an act or omission falling within the statutory description of Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
The existence of the requisite culpable mental state (intention, knowledge, rashness, or negligence) prescribed under Section 152.
The absence of any statutory justification, exception, or lawful authority under Chapter III (General Exceptions).
The resulting consequence or endangerment specified in the statutory formula of Section 152.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 152 is one of the most important legislative reforms in BNS 2023. It completely repeals and replaces Section 124A (Sedition) of the Indian Penal Code, dropping the controversial term 'sedition' and the colonial standard of 'disaffection'. Instead, Section 152 specifically targets concrete threats to national existence: purposely or knowingly exciting secession, armed rebellion, or subversive activities, encouraging separatist activities, or endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India by words, signs, visible representations, electronic communications, or financial means. Crucially, the statutory Explanation expressly protects democratic criticism: comments expressing disapprobation of government measures or administrative actions with a view to obtaining their alteration by lawful means do not constitute an offence.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of india under Section 152 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 152.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 152 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 152 BNS vs Colonial Sedition (IPC 124A): IPC 124A penalized 'disaffection' against the Government; Section 152 protects the 'sovereignty, unity and integrity of India' and targets secession and armed rebellion.

Section 152 vs Section 113 (Terrorist act): Section 113 targets violence designed to terrorize the public; Section 152 targets acts exciting secession, separatist movements, and subversive attacks on territorial unity.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 152 for conduct relating to act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of india.
Rule: Under BNS s. 152, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 152.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 152 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
